claims.text: The previously studied Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy shows limited amorphous retention.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a complex crystallization response during thermal analysis.
Substituting 1–5 at.% of phosphorus with boron will increase the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Substituting 1–5 at.% of phosphorus with boron will improve the alloy's thermal stability during reheating.
Cooling rates of approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s will promote formation of an amorphous phase in the modified alloy.
Boron addition will increase atomic-size mismatch in the alloy.
Boron addition will increase chemical disorder in the alloy.
Increased atomic-size mismatch and chemical disorder will enhance local structural frustration.
Enhanced local structural frustration will inhibit nucleation of crystalline phases during solidification and reheating.
Enhanced local structural frustration will inhibit growth of crystalline phases during solidification and reheating.
Boron has a substantially smaller atomic radius than the transition-metal constituents and phosphorus.
Boron has bonding characteristics different from those of the transition-metal constituents and phosphorus.
Boron can act as a network former and induce additional topological complexity in this alloy.
Boron-induced topological complexity will raise the nucleation barrier for crystallization.
The boron-modified alloy will have a broader cooling-rate process window for obtaining a fully amorphous structure than Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The beneficial effect is expected at cooling rates of at least approximately 10^5 K/s under moderate DSC reheating conditions.
The beneficial effect may not occur at substantially lower cooling rates.
The beneficial effect may not occur under extremely aggressive reheating conditions because crystallization kinetics will dominate.

contradictions.description: The nominal formula Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P(20–x)Bx defines substitution of boron for phosphorus while preserving 100 at.%, but the intervention alternatively describes boron as an additive component. An additive route would require renormalization and would not have the stated nominal composition.
